pr_title: net: tcp: Change locking order in connection establishment
pr_body:
When application calls TCP connect(), the call is blocked
by a semaphore which is then released when the connection
is established. Unfortunately the semaphore release was done
before the connection was marked as established. Depending
on the configuration options set, it is possible that after
the semaphore release, the thread that is waiting on connect()
is run immediately. Because of this, the connection bookeeping
still thought that the connection was not established even if
it was. A simple solution is to release the semaphore after
the connection is marked as established.

Fixes #35390

Signed-off-by: Jukka Rissanen <jukka.rissanen@linux.intel.com>

comments: This looks similar as #34923 but disabling the Ethernet controller did not help in this case.
This test is actually failing also for qemu_x86 and native_posix boards.
@rlubos do you know what this test is trying to do, any idea what might be the culprit?
AFAIR just some basic TLS handshake and exchanges, I can give a closer look at why does it fail.

Ok, so the test seems to be failing since f5fb80750e4f4ca9bbda08fe4ade95d9420bacf1 but I don't think it's the root cause of the failure, it rather just made the issue visible. The failure is caused by some weird scheduling happening in the networking stack.

Generally, the test uses loopback interface, with separate threads for the client and the server. What I observe is that the client thread, after leaving the `zsock_connect()` function on the underlying TCP socket, fails on the consecutive `zsock_send()` call, with `ENOTCONN` error. This happens, because when SYN/ACK from the server is received, the TCP2 will feed the `connect_sem` before actually setting its state to `TCP_ESTABLISHED` (https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/main/subsys/net/ip/tcp2.c#L1764). This makes the kernel reschedule threads, and the client thread takes precedence (the SYN/ACK was handled from the `rx_q[0]` thread).

Now, I think this behaviour of TCP2 is not correct anyway, as the RX queue thread or the network driver internal thread (in case RX queues are disabled) could be preemptive. What I don't understand though is why is the issue visible in this test suite. Both,  `rx_q[0]` and the client thread run on the same, cooperative priority (-1). My understanding is that the cooperative thread should only be "switched" if it becomes unready, and I believe feeding a semaphore is not such a condition? So `rx_q[0]` should rather have a chance to finish processing of the current packet instead of being preempted by the client thread. I don't feel confident enough to venture into kernel internals so I suggest to either look into TCP2 issue, as it doesn't seem to be hard to fix.

>  as it doesn't seem to be hard to fix.

Indeed the fix itself was trivial. Thanks for excellent analysis! :+1: 

This issue is a bit similar as #34964 but that one is related to server side timeouts in `recv()` (no exact culprit found yet for it), and this one was client side when doing a `connect()`

review_comments: Indeed this change seems to fix the issue in the TLS tests, but I'm wondering, the actual TCP state is updated at line 1933, shouldn't the semaphore be fed after that? In case a higher priority thread takes precendence after feeding the semaphore, it might still fail at `net_tcp_queue_data` which verifies the TCP internal state.
Hmm, that is a good point. Indeed the application might start to send more data even if the TCP has not yet fully finished the connection establishment. I will rework the PR more.
